macro.note: NYSE and Nasdaq both closed, confirmed on Nasdaq Trader's own market calendar. Knock-ons into the week, all confirmed: the Fed's H.10 foreign exchange release moves to Tuesday, and the EIA petroleum status report moves to Thursday at 12:00 PM. Natural gas storage does NOT move and stays Thursday 10:30 AM.

G.19 at 3:00 PM confirmed on the Fed's own September calendar and on the release masthead; Labor Day pushes the fifth business day to Tuesday. Census publishes TWO Quarterly Financial Reports at 10:00 AM, manufacturing/mining/wholesale/services and retail trade separately. Fed H.10 and H.15 both 4:15 PM, commercial paper 1:00 PM.

macro.event: ECB Governing Council Day 1, Berlin; 10yr reopening
macro.note: CORRECTION TO PRIOR RUNS: this is a MONETARY POLICY meeting, Day 1, hosted by the Bundesbank in Berlin - the ECB's own Governing Council calendar says so explicitly. Earlier briefs mislabelled it as a technical, non-policy meeting, which was wrong. BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation at 10:00 AM covers the JUNE reference period; Census Quarterly Services Survey also 10:00 AM. Treasury reopens the 10-year note at $39bn, competitive close 1:00 PM, now verified. The Bank of Canada does NOT announce this day - its September fixed date was the 2nd, where it held at 2.25%, and September 16 carries only the Summary of Deliberations at 1:30 PM ET.

Decision 8:15 AM ET and press conference 8:45 AM ET, both confirmed from the ECB's own published timing convention of 14:15 and 14:45 CET, and the venue is BERLIN rather than Frankfurt per the Governing Council calendar. FRAMING DISCIPLINE: a move to 2.50% is a poll EXPECTATION, not an ECB fact. Current ECB key rates are deposit 2.25%, main refinancing 2.40% and marginal lending 2.65%, effective 17 June 2026, and the 23 July decision HELD. Brief the direction as a HIKE if it comes - framing the ECB as easing is wrong by direction - but do not state it as scheduled fact.

macro.event: PPI, August; jobless claims; ORCL and ADBE after close
macro.note: NO GENUINE CONSENSUS POLL EXISTS for August PPI and this brief will not manufacture one. Reuters' own week-ahead piece carries a poll median for CPI only. What exists is a TradingEconomics vendor aggregate at +0.3% and a single-house Continuum Economics view at +0.4% headline / +0.3% core; neither is a poll median and neither should be called consensus. First of two inflation prints before the FOMC. Wholesale trade 10:00 AM, natural gas storage 10:30 AM, EIA petroleum shifted to 12:00 PM by the holiday. Treasury reopens the 30-year at $22bn, 1:00 PM. Oracle reports Q1 FY2027 and Adobe Q3 FY2026, both after the close, both confirmed from company sources.

macro.event: CPI, August - THE print the Fed named
macro.note: Reuters poll +0.4% headline and +0.2% core. The single most consequential scheduled release of the month and the last major inflation reading before the FOMC votes. Governor Waller said on September 3 that his decision will be heavily influenced by what we learn about August inflation - this is that reading, and it arrives with the Fed in blackout, so there will be no official reaction to it. Note the day: September 11 2026 is a FRIDAY, and any source dating August CPI to a Wednesday is prior-year copy. Real Earnings also 8:30 AM, University of Michigan preliminary sentiment 10:00 AM, Business Formation Statistics 10:00 AM, Fed Z.1 Financial Accounts 12:00 PM.

The 9/4 cohort prices 42.6% hold against 57.4% for a 25bp HIKE, and the probability of a CUT is exactly zero at every meeting through March 2027. Other estimates span 51% to 65%, so brief it as a range rather than a point. The 2:00 PM statement time is solid from 2026 precedent - every 2026 statement carried a 2:00 p.m. release header. CORRECTION TO RUN #173: the 2:30 PM press-conference time is NOT confirmed for September 16; the Fed has not posted a press-conference page for that date, so 2:30 PM is the standing convention and remains unverified for this meeting. The Bank of Japan meets September 17-18 and is widely expected to hike, statement time unpublished. The Fed communications blackout runs September 5 through September 17.

earnings.note: Oracle reports first quarter fiscal 2027 after the close on September 10, confirmed from company investor relations. The most consequential single earnings report of the week as a read on AI infrastructure demand and backlog conversion - and it lands the evening before CPI, into a market that has just repriced the policy path higher. No weekend news or preview was found.

Adobe reports third quarter fiscal 2026 after the close on September 10. Read as a check on whether software that monetises AI usage is still being rewarded. Citi published an achievable set-up note on September 2 with a raised price target; nothing new emerged over the weekend.
